summary: Serverless/BaaS architecture: Firebase serving React + Vite (SPA) (web) + React Native (Expo) for Android + iOS, hosted on Cloudflare (Workers static assets / Pages). Estimated $23,300-44,800/month (above the $0 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: Firebase provides data, auth and APIs as managed services; custom logic runs as functions, so there is no server fleet to operate. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 1 engineer(s), no DevOps cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.choice: React + Vite (SPA) (web) + React Native (Expo) for Android + iOS
frontend.justification: Web - React + Vite (SPA): Chosen because team already works in javascript (team.languages); strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; shares React/TypeScript skills and code with the React Native (Expo) app; rich client-side interactivity for a social. Mobile - React Native (Expo): Chosen because team already works in javascript (team.languages); one codebase ships both Android and iOS (project.platforms); strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3; gentle learning curve suits a beginner team on a 4-week timeline.

alternatives.why_not: React + Vite scores higher on platform coverage (fit 8.7 vs 8.9).
React Native scores higher on maintainability and performance (fit 8.9 vs 9.3).

tradeoffs: Routing/data fetching choices left to the team
Some native modules need custom development builds

backend.justification: Chosen because team already works in javascript (team.languages); gentle learning curve suits a beginner team on a 4-week timeline; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3. Accepted trade-off: complex social workflows outgrow BaaS rules and edge functions.

Firebase scores higher on learning curve and scalability (fit 8.1 vs 9.2).

tradeoffs: Proprietary data model and APIs (high lock-in)
Firebase Authentication offers no data-location choice
Weak at relational queries and reporting

database.justification: Chosen because Firebase is built on Cloud Firestore; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3. Accepted trade-off: money/relational data needs multi-row ACID guarantees. Managed as Cloud Firestore: fully managed: no operations work for a team without DevOps; managed failover/standby available.

tradeoffs: Limited querying/joins; reporting needs exports

warnings.message: availability=99.99 (~4.3 min downtime/month) needs multi-region failover and 24x7 on-call; a 1-person beginner team without DevOps cannot operate that.

Estimated minimum $23,300/month exceeds budget.monthly_infra_usd=$0. Biggest drivers: Firebase Authentication (~$19,058), Cloud Firestore (~$3,625). The stack shown is already the cost-optimised plan.
Scope (~13.5 feature points: 3 platform(s), social domain, requirements) far exceeds capacity (1 beginner engineer(s) x 4 weeks). Ship one platform first.
5,000,000 users with 1 engineer(s): only fully managed, autoscaling services are viable.
3 client platforms in 4 weeks: cross-platform code sharing is assumed; consider launching on one platform first.
99.99% needs active-active or warm-standby in a second region; the stack is multi-zone in one region (~99.95%) plus cross-region replicas. Budget for the second region.
250,000 concurrent realtime connections: run a dedicated, horizontally scaled connection tier.
Cloud Firestore is proprietary; migrating away later means rewriting the data layer.
Firebase (Firestore + Auth + Functions) is proprietary; migrating away later means rewriting the data layer.

assumptions: No data_residency or user geography given; primary region defaults to US East (move it next to your users)
Budget re-plan attempted (cost weighted at 5) but no cheaper compliant plan exists
RELAXED budget.monthly_infra_usd: requirements as stated need at least ~$23,300/month; raise the budget or reduce scope (fewer platforms, lower availability, defer search/realtime features)
RELAXED requirements.availability: designed for ~99.95% on managed multi-zone services (provider SLAs) instead of self-operated 99.99% multi-region failover
RELAXED timeline.mvp_weeks: phase the MVP - first platform and core flow only; cross-platform frameworks were preferred to limit the number of codebases
